newsitem.title: FRANCE: Barley stocks lower in draft French grain report.
newsitem.headline: Barley stocks lower in draft French grain report.

text.p: A cut in closing barley stocks is among the few changes expected in a new supply/demand report on French cereals this week, industry sources said on Monday.

Cereals office ONIC, in the draft of a monthly report due for release on Wednesday, proposes to cut its forecast for 1996/97 carryover barley stocks to 905,000 tonnes from a previous estimate of 1.045 million tonnes, the sources said.
The change stems partly from an increase of 50,000 tonnes in off-farm consumption on the domestic market this season -- to 1.635 million tonnes from 1.585 million.
ONIC also plans to revise up exports to other European Union countries to 2.37 million tonnes from 2.28 million. Its non-EU export goal remains unchanged at 1.5 million.
The figures for the season ending on June 30 are provisional and must be cleared by a full ONIC committee before publication.
Barley stocks began the July/June season at 626,000 tonnes.
Production rose last year to a revised 9.497 million tonnes from a 1995 harvest of 7.739 million, ONIC is expected to say.
For soft or common wheat, ONIC is expected to keep most key categories unchanged except for intra-EU exports -- up 50,000 tonnes from the previous projection to 9.185 million tonnes.
Last year's production is revised up to 34.657 million tonnes from 24.578 million for a closing stock figure of 2.021 million tonnes compared with the previous forecast of 2.061.
The draft for maize shows a dip in previously expected closing stocks to 2.479 million tonnes from 2.519 million.
Exports within the 15-nation EU are revised up to 6.435 million tonnes from 6.0 million and third-country exports shaved to 100,000 tonnes.
Internal market consumption is trimmed to 3.686 million from 3.736 million tonnes estimated in March, and 2.6 million tonnes of the new total is for manufactured animal feed.
The 1996 maize crop was 14.305 million tonnes, up slightly from 14.280 million previously reckoned, industry sources said.
